[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Customer extensions need to be packaged and distributed as independently deployable micro-frontend modules. Without standardized Webpack Module Federation configuration, extensions cannot be dynamically loaded at runtime, properly version dependencies, or efficiently share code with host applications, resulting in 3-6 month deployment cycles, 800KB+ bundle duplication, and incompatibility issues across 50+ state implementations.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Standardize packaging customer extensions as Webpack 5 Module Federation remote modules with versioned CDN entry points, shared dependency configuration (React, design system), dynamic remote loading infrastructure, and automated deployment pipelines. Enables independent extension deployment (2-day cycle), runtime composition based on tenant context, and 60% bundle size reduction through shared dependencies.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

Apply this pattern when:
- Packaging customer extensions as independently deployable micro-frontends (Texas claims validator, California provider dashboard)
- Enabling dynamic runtime loading of tenant-specific UI extensions per PTN-APP-MTN-012
- Managing independent versioning of extensions from core product (extension v2.1 with host v6.3)
- Supporting multi-tenant SaaS with customer-specific UI modules (50+ states, each with 3-8 extensions)
- Extensions >50KB requiring code splitting and lazy loading
- Multiple extension teams deploying independently
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Independent Deployment**: Extensions deploy to CDN separately from host, eliminating full product rebuild cycles
- **Runtime Composition**: Extensions load dynamically based on tenant/user context; Texas sees Texas extensions only
- **Version Flexibility**: Extensions and host maintain independent version lifecycles; extension v2.1 works with host v6.2-6.4
- **Code Sharing**: Shared dependencies (React, design system) loaded once, significantly reducing bundle size duplication
- **Rollback Safety**: Extension rollback independent of host; change CDN URL to previous version
- **Team Autonomy**: Teams deploy without coordination for faster release velocity

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineer**: Configures and maintains Webpack Module Federation infrastructure, CDN distribution, and dynamic loading pipelines.
- **Application Architect**: Designs the federated module architecture, shared dependency strategy, and extension registry.
- **.NET Developer**: Packages extensions as Module Federation remotes and configures independent deployment pipelines.
- **DDI Engineer**: Uses Module Federation to deploy tenant-specific UI extensions independently from core product releases.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Customer extensions drive significant revenue across multiple state contracts. Each state deploys multiple custom extensions (claims validation, provider workflows, eligibility checks). Extensions require independent deployment from core product releases.

**Long Deployment Cycles**: Current monolithic packaging requires full product rebuild and regression testing for any extension change. A simple bug fix in an extension can take months to reach production, generating customer escalations.

**Bundle Duplication**: Extensions that bundle all dependencies (React, design system, routing libraries) separately create significant duplicate payload across tenants, degrading initial page load performance.

**Version Incompatibility**: Extensions locked to specific host versions break when the host upgrades. A significant portion of extensions require rework during host upgrades, increasing maintenance costs.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

**Webpack 5 Module Federation**: Gainwell migrated to Webpack 5 enabling Module Federation for runtime micro-frontend composition. Host applications configure remote entry points; extensions expose components dynamically loaded.

**CDN Distribution**: Azure CDN hosts extension bundles at versioned URLs (https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/texas-claims/v2.1.3/remoteEntry.js). Cache-Control headers enable versioning; host fetches specific versions.

**Shared Dependencies**: Module Federation singleton configuration ensures React, design system, React Router loaded once by host; extensions consume shared instances. Reduces bundle size from 800KB to 180KB per extension.

**12 React-Ready Products**: ClaimsPro, MMIS Portal, ProviderConnect, and 9 others support Module Federation extensions. 522 legacy ASP.NET apps incompatible (require migration).

**Extension SDK**: @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react (v2.4, 120KB) provides loadRemoteModule() helper, error boundaries, fallback UI for failed remote loads.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

**Problem 1: Monolithic Deployment Requires Full Rebuild**
_Symptom_: Texas fixes claims validator bug; requires full MMIS Portal rebuild, regression testing, coordinated release.
_Root Cause_: Extensions bundled into host application; no independent deployment mechanism.
_Impact_: Bug fix delayed for months; customer escalation.

**Problem 2: Duplicate Dependencies Bloat Bundle Size**
_Symptom_: Each extension bundles React (420KB gzipped), design system (320KB), React Router (60KB).
_Root Cause_: No shared dependency mechanism; Webpack bundles all imports.
_Impact_: Significant payload duplication across extensions; slow initial page load; user complaints.

**Problem 3: Version Incompatibility During Host Upgrades**
_Symptom_: Texas extension built against host v6.2; host upgrades to v6.4; extension breaks (React Context API change).
_Root Cause_: Tight coupling between extension and host versions; no compatibility buffer.
_Impact_: Significant portion of extensions require rework after host upgrades; increased maintenance burden.

**Problem 4: No Runtime Tenant-Specific Loading (security risk)**
_Symptom_: All extensions load for all tenants; Texas sees California extensions in browser DevTools.
_Root Cause_: Static bundling; no dynamic loading based on tenant context.
_Impact_: Intellectual property exposure; unnecessary bundle downloading; security audit concern.

**Problem 5: Rollback Complexity**
_Symptom_: Extension deployment causes bug; rollback requires full host application rollback.
_Root Cause_: Extensions bundled with host; no independent rollback mechanism.
_Impact_: Lengthy rollback process; production outage risk; emergency change approval required.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

**Competing Forces:**
- **Independence vs Coordination**: Extensions need autonomy but must align with host API contracts
- **Performance vs Flexibility**: Dynamic loading adds latency; static bundling optimizes load time
- **Versioning vs Stability**: Flexible versioning enables agility but risks incompatibility

**Hard Constraints:**
- **Webpack 5+ Required**: Module Federation unavailable in older bundlers; 12 products support, 522 legacy apps don't
- **Shared Dependency Versions**: Extensions must use compatible React/design system versions (±1 minor)
- **CDN Infrastructure**: Requires Azure CDN deployment pipeline; global distribution; cache invalidation
- **Bundle Size <100KB**: Per-extension limit to maintain performance; gzipped after shared dependencies
- **CORS Compliance**: CDN must serve with proper CORS headers for cross-origin module loading
- **Backward Compatibility**: Extensions must support host ±1 minor version (v6.2 extension works with v6.1-6.3 host)

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

**Module Federation Extension Packaging** configures customer extensions as Webpack 5 remote modules with: (1) webpack.config.js ModuleFederationPlugin exposing components, (2) Shared dependency configuration (React, design system as singletons), (3) remoteEntry.js entry point deployed to versioned CDN URL, (4) Dynamic loading infrastructure in host using import() and loadRemoteModule() helper, (5) Automated deployment pipeline publishing to Azure CDN.

**Key Principles:**
1. **Remote Module Exposure**: Extensions export components via exposes config; host dynamically imports
2. **Singleton Shared Dependencies**: React, design system marked singleton=true; loaded once by host
3. **Versioned CDN URLs**: Each extension version published to unique URL; cache-busting via query param
4. **Dynamic Tenant Loading**: Host fetches tenant-specific extension URLs from registry; loads runtime
5. **Fallback Handling**: Error boundaries catch failed remote loads; display fallback UI
6. **Independent Deployment**: Extensions deploy to CDN without host rebuild; 2-day cycle

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component   | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------ |
| **Remote Module (Extension)** | Webpack-built extension exposing components via ModuleFederationPlugin; deployed to CDN as remoteEntry.js + chunks | Webpack 5+, React 18+, TypeScript |
| **Module Federation Config (webpack.config.js)** | Defines extension name, exposes entries, shared dependencies (React/design system singletons), remote entry filename | ModuleFederationPlugin, package.json |
| **Remote Entry Point (remoteEntry.js)** | Webpack-generated entry script containing module metadata, dependency manifest, chunk URLs for lazy loading | Webpack Module Federation runtime |
| **Shared Dependencies (React, Design System)** | Libraries marked singleton=true; host provides single instance; extensions consume without bundling | React 18+, @gainwell/design-system-react |
| **Extension Registry** | Backend service mapping tenant IDs to extension URLs; host queries for tenant-specific extensions | PostgreSQL, REST API |
| **Dynamic Loader (loadRemoteModule)** | SDK helper loading remote modules at runtime; handles errors, fallbacks, version compatibility checks | @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react |
| **CI/CD Deployment Pipeline** | Azure DevOps pipeline building extension, publishing to CDN with versioned URL, updating registry | Azure DevOps, Azure CDN |

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

**Build and Deployment Flow:**
1. Developer commits extension code to Git repository
2. CI/CD pipeline triggers webpack build with Module Federation config
3. Webpack generates remoteEntry.js + chunk files (total <100KB gzipped)
4. Pipeline deploys to Azure CDN at versioned URL (https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/texas-claims/v2.1.3/)
5. Pipeline updates Extension Registry with tenant-to-URL mapping

**Runtime Loading Flow:**
1. User (Texas tenant) logs into host application
2. Host queries Extension Registry for tenant-specific extensions (returns texas-claims v2.1.3 URL)
3. Host dynamically imports remoteEntry.js: `import('https://cdn.gainwell.com/.../remoteEntry.js')`
4. Webpack Module Federation runtime loads remoteEntry, checks shared dependencies
5. Extension consumes host-provided React/design system (no duplicate loading)
6. Extension component renders in host application UI

**Error Handling Flow:**
1. Remote module load fails (CDN timeout, 404, JavaScript error)
2. loadRemoteModule() helper catches error
3. Error boundary displays fallback UI ("Extension unavailable")
4. Telemetry logs error with extension ID, tenant, version, stack trace
5. Host application continues functioning; other extensions unaffected

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Variation 1: Static Remote Configuration**
Host hardcodes extension URLs in webpack.config.js remotes. Simple but requires host rebuild for version changes. Suitable for single-tenant deployments or controlled environments.

**Variation 2: Dynamic Registry-Based Loading**
Host fetches extension URLs from database registry at runtime. No host rebuild for version updates. Suitable for multi-tenant SaaS (50+ states). This pattern uses this variation.

**Variation 3: Extension Marketplace**
Tenants browse/install extensions from marketplace UI. Registry updated via admin portal. Enables self-service extension management. Adds complexity.

**Variation 4: Versioned Shared Scope**
Extensions specify compatible host version ranges (^6.2.0). Host validates compatibility before loading. Prevents incompatible extension loading. Recommended for production.

### Prerequisites

Before implementing Module Federation extensions:

- **Webpack 5.60+**: Module Federation requires Webpack 5.60 or later; verify with `webpack --version`
- **Node.js 18+ and npm 9+**: For build tooling and dependency management
- **React 18+ and TypeScript 4.5+**: Extensions must use compatible React version (±1 minor from host)
- **Azure CDN Access**: Deployment credentials for publishing extension bundles to https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/
- **Extension Registry API Access**: Credentials for updating tenant-to-URL mappings in Extension Registry
- **@gainwell/extensions-sdk-react v2.4+**: For loadRemoteModule() helper and ExtensionComponentProps interface

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#phase-1-extension-module-federation-setup]

#### Phase 1: Extension Module Federation Setup

**Step 1: Configure webpack.config.js for remote module**
Create webpack.config.js in extension project root. Add ModuleFederationPlugin configuring:
- **name**: Unique extension identifier (e.g., 'texasClaimsExtension')
- **filename**: 'remoteEntry.js' (Webpack-generated entry point)
- **exposes**: Component paths to expose (e.g., './ClaimsValidator': './src/components/ClaimsValidator')
- **shared**: Dependencies marked as singletons (React, React-DOM, design system with requiredVersion constraints)

**Step 2: Define exposed modules and components**
List all extension components to expose in exposes config. Use relative paths from project root. Example:
- './ClaimsValidator': './src/components/ClaimsValidator'
- './EligibilityWidget': './src/components/EligibilityWidget'

Host will import using: `const ClaimsValidator = await loadRemoteModule('texasClaimsExtension', './ClaimsValidator')`

**Step 3: Configure shared dependencies**
Mark React, React-DOM, and design system as shared with singleton=true and requiredVersion. This prevents duplicate loading. Host provides these libraries; extension consumes them. Use ±1 minor version range for compatibility.

**Step 4: Set up remote entry point**
Configure filename: 'remoteEntry.js'. Webpack auto-generates this file containing module metadata, dependency manifest, and chunk URLs. Deploy this to CDN as main entry point. See Example 1 below for complete configuration.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#phase-2-build-and-deployment-pipeline]

#### Phase 2: Build and Deployment Pipeline

**Step 1: Create build pipeline for extension**
Create Azure DevOps azure-pipelines.yml in extension repo. Configure triggers (main branch commits), build steps (npm install → webpack build → tests), and CDN deployment. Extract version from package.json for URL versioning.

Example pipeline YAML:
```yaml
trigger:
  - main
steps:
- task: NodeTool@0
  inputs:
    versionSpec: '18.x'
- script: npm ci && npm run build && npm test
- task: AzureFileCopy@4  # Deploy to CDN
  inputs:
    SourcePath: 'dist/*'
    Destination: 'AzureBlob'
    ContainerName: 'extensions'
    BlobPrefix: 'texas-claims/v$(cat package.json | jq -r .version)/'
```

**Step 2: Configure asset deployment to CDN**
Deploy dist/ folder to Azure CDN at versioned URL: https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/{extension-name}/v{version}/. Configure CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://*.gainwell.com) and Cache-Control (public, max-age=31536000, immutable for 1-year cache).

**Step 3: Set up versioning strategy**
Use semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) from package.json. Each version deployed to unique CDN path. No URL overwrites; old versions remain accessible for rollback. Update Extension Registry API with new version URL after deployment.

**Step 4: Implement deployment automation**
Pipeline runs on commit to main. Automatically: builds extension, runs tests, deploys to CDN, updates registry API. Manual approval optional for production deployments. Deployment time: 3-5 minutes.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#phase-3-host-application-integration]

#### Phase 3: Host Application Integration

**Step 1: Configure host to consume remote modules**
Update host webpack.config.js with ModuleFederationPlugin. Configure shared dependencies (React, design system) as singletons. Use empty remotes: {} for dynamic loading or specify static URLs. Ensure singleton=true to share libraries with extensions.

**Step 2: Implement dynamic import() logic**
Create loadTenantExtensions() function:
1. Query Extension Registry API: GET /extensions?tenantId=texas
2. Receive URLs: [{id: 'texas-claims', url: 'https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/texas-claims/v2.1.3/remoteEntry.js'}]
3. Dynamically import: await import(extensionUrl)
4. Extract component: const Component = await loadRemoteModule({remoteUrl, scope: 'texasClaimsExtension', module: './ClaimsValidator'})
5. Render component in host UI

See Example 3 below for complete TypeScript implementation.

**Step 3: Add fallback handling**
Wrap extension loading in try/catch. Use error boundaries to catch rendering errors. Display fallback UI on failure: "Extension unavailable. Please contact support." Log errors to telemetry with extension ID, version, tenant, error message. Host continues functioning; other extensions unaffected.

**Step 4: Test end-to-end integration**
Test scenarios:
- Extension loads successfully for configured tenant
- Extension does not load for unconfigured tenant
- CDN timeout handled gracefully (5-second timeout, fallback UI)
- Extension version upgrade (deploy v2.1.4, verify host loads new version without rebuild)
- Rollback (revert registry to v2.1.3 URL, verify host loads previous version)
- Shared dependencies (verify React loaded once, check browser DevTools Network tab)

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

**1. Use Semantic Versioning for Extension Releases**
Version extensions as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (e.g., 2.1.3). Breaking changes increment MAJOR (API changes), new features increment MINOR (backward compatible), bug fixes increment PATCH. Deploy each version to unique CDN URL. Host specifies compatible version range (^2.1.0 accepts 2.1.x, 2.2.x but not 3.0.0).

**2. Configure Shared Dependencies as Singletons**
Mark React, React-DOM, design system as singleton: true in both host and extension webpack configs. Prevents duplicate loading (saves 740KB). Use requiredVersion to enforce compatibility ('^18.0.0'). Host loads libraries once; extensions consume shared instances.

**3. Implement Proper Error Handling for Failed Remote Loads**
Wrap dynamic import() in try/catch. Use React error boundaries to catch rendering errors. Display fallback UI: "Extension unavailable." Log errors to Application Insights with extension ID, version, tenant, error stack. Set 5-second timeout for remote loads. Test CDN timeout scenarios (disconnect network during load).

**4. Use CDN for Hosting Extension Bundles**
Deploy extensions to Azure CDN with global distribution. Configure Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000 for versioned URLs (immutable). Use CORS headers: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://*.gainwell.com. Monitor  cache hit ratio (target >95%). CDN reduces load time from 2000ms (origin server) to 80-150ms.

**5. Minimize Bundle Size Through Code Splitting**
Use dynamic import() for large dependencies. Webpack automatically splits into chunks. Target <100KB per extension (gzipped, after shared deps). Analyze with webpack-bundle-analyzer. Remove unused imports (tree-shaking). Avoid bundling images/fonts; serve from CDN separately.

**6. Version Remote Entry URLs for Cache Busting**
Include version in CDN URL: /extensions/texas-claims/v2.1.3/remoteEntry.js. Never overwrite URLs. Old versions remain for rollback. Update Extension Registry API with new version URL. Host fetches URL from registry; client caches aggressively (1-year Cache-Control).

**7. Test Extensions with Multiple Host Application Versions**
Extensions must support host ±1 minor version (extension v2.1 works with host v6.2, v6.3, v6.4). Test matrix: extension v2.1.x with host v6.2, v6.3, v6.4. Use feature detection for API compatibility. Document minimum host version in README.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

**1. Shared Dependency Version Mismatches Causing Runtime Errors**
_Problem_: Extension built with React 18.2, host uses React 18.1. Extension calls API added in 18.2; host crashes with "undefined is not a function."
_Root Cause_: Misaligned React versions; extension bundles newer React but host provides older singleton.
_Solution_: Use requiredVersion with range ('^18.0.0' accepts 18.0-18.x). Test extension with minimum and maximum host versions. CI pipeline checks host React version compatibility.
_Example_: California extension shipped React 18.3 Context API; host v6.2 runs React 18.0; 42 tenant crashes in production.

**2. Missing Fallback Handling When Remote Module Fails to Load**
_Problem_: CDN down; remote module DNS timeout; white screen; no error message; users report "application broken."
_Root Cause_: No try/catch around dynamic import(); no error boundary; unhandled promise rejection crashes app.
_Solution_: Wrap import() in try/catch. Use React error boundary. Display fallback UI: "Extension unavailable. Core functionality still available." Set 5-second timeout.
_Example_: Texas CDN outage (2 hours); host application crashed entirely; users unable to process claims.

**3. Large Bundle Sizes Due to Not Sharing Dependencies Properly**
_Problem_: Extension bundle 820KB; includes React (420KB), design system (320KB), lodash (80KB); slow load time.
_Root Cause_: Shared dependencies not configured as singleton; Webpack bundles everything.
_Solution_: Mark React, React-DOM, design system as shared: { singleton: true }. Use peerDependencies in package.json. Verify with webpack-bundle-analyzer (target <100KB).
_Example_: Florida eligibility extension 780KB before; 92KB after shared dependency config; 88% reduction.

**4. CORS Issues When Loading Remotes from Different Domains**
_Problem_: Host at https://mmis.gainwell.com loads extension from https://cdn.gainwell.com; browser blocks with "CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header."
_Root Cause_: CDN missing CORS headers; browser security blocks cross-origin scripts.
_Solution_: Configure Azure CDN with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://*.gainwell.com. Test with curl -I command. Verify in browser DevTools Network tab.
_Example_: California deployment blocked in production; 4-hour incident; emergency CDN config change.

**5. Cache Invalidation Problems with Static Remote URLs**
_Problem_: Deploy extension v2.1.4; users still load v2.1.3 from browser cache; old code executes.
_Root Cause_: URL unchanged (/remoteEntry.js); browser caches with 1-year Cache-Control; no cache busting.
_Solution_: Version URLs (/v2.1.4/remoteEntry.js). Never overwrite. Update registry with new URL. Cache aggressively on versioned URLs; purge CDN cache on deploy.
_Example_: Texas bug fix deployed; users report bug persists; cache causing 18-hour delay in fix propagation.

**6. Breaking Changes in Exposed Module Interfaces Without Versioning**
_Problem_: Extension v2.2 changes ClaimsValidator component props (removed onValidate callback); host still passes onValidate; TypeScript error bypassed in production; runtime error.
_Root Cause_: No interface versioning; breaking change deployed without host coordination.
_Solution_: Use semantic versioning (MAJOR for breaking changes). Document API contracts in README. Deprecate props before removal (2-version grace period). Test with multiple host versions.
_Example_: California provider extension v3.0 broke 12 host integrations; emergency rollback; lost 2 days.

### Standards Alignment

This pattern aligns with and extends:

- **[PTN-APP-EXT-003: Customization Package Management](PTN-APP-EXT-003-customization-package-management-pattern.md)**: Module Federation packages deployed as npm packages to Azure Artifacts; extensions follow same versioning and dependency management standards
- **[PTN-APP-EXT-012: React Component Extension](PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md)**: Federated extensions expose React components conforming to ExtensionComponentProps interface; error boundaries, theme provider integration required
- **[PTN-APP-MTN-012: Tenant Micro-Frontend Loading](../../multi-tenancy/PTN-APP-MTN-012-tenant-micro-frontend-loading-pattern.md)**: Extensions load dynamically based on tenant configuration; Extension Registry maps tenants to remote entry URLs
- **[Enterprise Micro-Frontend Architecture Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-micro-frontend-architecture.md)**: Module Federation is standard micro-frontend implementation; all new extensions must use this pattern

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

**Security Compliance:**
- **CDN Security**: Azure CDN serves extensions over HTTPS only; TLS 1.2+ required
- **Subresource Integrity (SRI)**: Optional for production; generate integrity hashes for remoteEntry.js; browser validates before execution
- **Content Security Policy (CSP)**: Extensions must not violate host CSP headers; no inline scripts, eval(), or external domains
- **PHI Protection**: Extensions must not bundle PHI/PII in JavaScript; load sensitive data via API calls only

**Accessibility Compliance:**
- Extensions must meet WCAG 2.2 AA standards per PTN-APP-EXT-012
- Use Gainwell Design System components for accessibility by default
- Test with axe-core; zero violations required for production deployment

**Performance Compliance:**
- Remote module load time <500ms (95th percentile)
- Bundle size <100KB gzipped per extension
- Failed remote loads <0.5% (measure with Application Insights)
- Shared dependency cache hit rate >95%

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

**Architecture Review Board (ARB) Approval Required:**  \n1. **Submit Extension Proposal**: Extension architect submits proposal with business justification, technical design (webpack config, exposed modules), bundle size estimate, deployment plan  \n2. **ARB Review (2 weeks)**: Board reviews: (a) Module Federation compliance, (b) Shared dependency configuration, (c) Bundle size <100KB target, (d) CORS/CSP compatibility, (e) Error handling (fallbacks, error boundaries), (f) Versioning strategy  \n3. **Security Audit (1 week)**: Security team reviews: (a) PHI/PII not bundled, (b) CDN HTTPS configuration, (c) CSP compliance, (d) No vulnerable dependencies (npm audit)  \n4. **Approval and Deployment**: ARB approves? Proceed to CI/CD pipeline deployment. Rejected? Address concerns, resubmit.  \n5. **Post-Deployment Validation (72 hours)**: Monitor metrics (load time, error rate, bundle size). ARB reviews metrics; approves production rollout.

**Fast-Track for Minor Updates:**  \nPatch versions (2.1.3 → 2.1.4) bypass ARB if: (a) No API changes, (b) Bundle size delta <10KB, (c) Automated tests pass. Architect self-approves; deploys directly.

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric   | Target       | Measurement Method |
| -------- | ------------ | ------------------ |
| Remote module load time | <500ms (p95) | Application Insights custom metric tracking import() duration from initiation to module resolution |
| Failed remote loads | <0.5% | Error telemetry counting try/catch exceptions during loadRemoteModule(); alert if >0.5% over 1-hour window |
| Bundle size per extension | <100KB gzipped | Webpack bundle analysis in CI/CD pipeline; build fails if >100KB; webpack-bundle-analyzer report archived |
| Shared dependency cache hit rate | >95% | Browser Performance API tracking resource timing; cache hits (transferSize=0) vs total requests; dashboard in Grafana |

**Alerting:**  \n- Failed remote loads >1% for 15 minutes → PagerDuty alert to on-call engineer  \n- Remote module load time >1000ms (p95) for 30 minutes → Slack alert to #extensions-team  \n- CDN error rate >0.1% → Automatic CDN health check; escalate to Azure support if CDN down

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (FAHCA) required custom provider credentialing workflow extension for Medicaid MMIS Portal. Florida has unique 42-step credentialing process (vs. standard 18 steps). Extension needed independent deployment without impacting other states. Previous monolithic approach required 4-month releases.

**Implementation:**
1. **Module Federation Configuration**: Created @gainwell-extensions/florida-credentialing package. Configured webpack.config.js with ModuleFederationPlugin exposing 3 components: CredentialingWizard (multi-step form), DocumentUpload (file management), StatusDashboard (application tracking). Shared React 18.2, design system v4.1, React Router v6.8.
2. **CDN Deployment**: Azure DevOps pipeline builds extension on commit to main branch. Deploys to https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/florida-credentialing/v1.3.2/ with remoteEntry.js (12KB) + 4 chunks (total 87KB gzipped). Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000.
3. **Dynamic Loading**: MMIS Portal queries Extension Registry for tenant "florida-mmis". Registry returns URL. Host dynamically imports: `await loadRemoteModule({remoteUrl: 'https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/florida-credentialing/v1.3.2/remoteEntry.js', scope: 'floridaCredentialing', module: './CredentialingWizard'})`. Extension renders in Portal Settings > Provider Management section.
4. **Error Handling**: Wrapped in error boundary. CDN timeout triggers fallback UI: "Credentialing extension unavailable. Contact support." Application Insights logs errors with extension ID, version, tenant.

**Outcome:**
- **Deployment Cycle**: 6 weeks → 2 days (97% reduction). Florida deploys credentialing fixes without coordinating with core product releases.
- **Bundle Size**: 780KB → 87KB (89% reduction). Shared React/design system loaded once by host.
- **Load Performance**: Extension renders in 180ms (CDN cache hit). Florida users report "instant" load compared to previous 8-second full page reload.
- **Independent Versioning**: Florida runs extension v1.3.2 while Texas runs v1.2.8. No conflict. Different credentialing requirements isolated.
- **Rollback Speed**: Bug in v1.3.3 detected. Registry updated to v1.3.2 URL. Rollback in 90 seconds (vs. 12-hour monolith rollback).

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) required real-time claims validation extension for ClaimsPro application. California has 180+ specialized claim validation rules (vs. standard 60). Rules change quarterly per state legislation. Previous approach bundled validators; any rule change triggered full ClaimsPro rebuild (3-month release cycle).

**Implementation:**
1. **Module Federation Setup**: Created @gainwell-extensions/california-claims-validator package. Webpack config exposes ClaimsValidator component (React functional component with 180 rule functions). Shared dependencies: React 18.2, design system v4.2, lodash-es (tree-shaken). peerDependencies prevent bundling.
2. **Build Pipeline**: Azure DevOps pipeline: (a) Runs 420 unit tests (Jest + React Testing Library), (b) Builds with webpack --mode production (minification, tree-shaking), (c) Generates bundle analysis report (56KB gzipped after shared deps), (d) Deploys to CDN https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/california-claims/v2.4.1/, (e) Updates Extension Registry API: `POST /extensions {extensionId: 'california-claims', version: '2.4.1', tenantId: 'california-dhcs', url: '...'}`, (f) Sends Slack notification to #california-team.
3. **Dynamic Loading in ClaimsPro**: ClaimsPro loads extension at runtime: (a) User (California tenant) navigates to Claims Submission page, (b) App queries registry: `GET /extensions?tenantId=california-dhcs&feature=claims-validation`, (c) Receives URL, (d) Dynamically imports: `const {ClaimsValidator} = await import(remoteUrl)`, (e) Renders validator in claim form. Texas users navigate to same page; no California extension loaded (registry returns empty array).
4. **Shared Dependency Optimization**: ClaimsPro ModuleFederationPlugin config marks React, design system as singleton. California extension consumes host-provided instances, significantly reducing total bundle size compared to previous monolithic bundling.
5. **Error Handling**: Extension wrapped in error boundary. Timeout set to 5 seconds. CDN failure displays: "Claims validation unavailable. Submit claim for manual review." Fallback workflow allows claim submission without real-time validation; backend validators still run.

**Outcome:**
- **Deployment Frequency**: Quarterly (3 months) → Weekly (7 days). Rule changes deploy immediately without ClaimsPro rebuild.
- **Time-to-Production**: Rule change request → production deployment: 12 weeks → 3 days (96% reduction). Quarterly legislative changes no longer cause deployment bottlenecks.
- **Failed Load Rate**: 0.08% (p95). 8 failures per 10,000 requests. Error boundary catches; fallback UI works. Zero user-impacting outages.
- **Load Performance**: Extension load time 120ms (p95) from CDN. 420ms from origin server (cold cache). Cache hit rate 97.2%.
- **Version Flexibility**: California runs validator v2.4.1. Host ClaimsPro v5.8. Independent versions. California requested new rule; deployed validator v2.4.2 without host upgrade. Texas continued running ClaimsPro v5.8 with Texas validator v1.9.3.
- **Cost Savings**: Eliminated rule deployment escalation costs. Reduced development churn (no full regression testing for rule changes).
- **Scalability**: Pattern replicated for Texas, Florida, Ohio. 4 states now deploy independent claim validators. ClaimsPro supports 12+ validators without code changes.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#scenario-1-single-tenant-extension-deployment]

#### Scenario 1: Single Tenant Extension Deployment

**Situation**: Texas HHSC needs custom prior authorization workflow extension for MMIS Portal. Workflow unique to Texas; no other state requires it. Extension must deploy independently to support Texas regulatory changes (quarterly updates).

**Application**: Configure Texas prior auth extension as Module Federation remote. Webpack config exposes PriorAuthWizard component. Deploy to CDN at /extensions/texas-prior-auth/v1.2.0/. Extension Registry maps tenant "texas-hhsc" to this URL. MMIS Portal queries registry with tenant ID; dynamically imports extension only for Texas users. Other states see no prior auth extension.

**Benefit**: Texas-specific logic isolated. Quarterly regulatory changes deploy to Texas without impacting California, Florida, Ohio. Independent deployment cycle (2-3 days vs. 3-6 month coordinated release). Extension versioned separately (v1.2.0 while host at v6.4).
page_texts.43:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#scenario-2-multi-tenant-dynamic-extension-loading]

#### Scenario 2: Multi-Tenant Dynamic Extension Loading

**Situation**: ClaimsPro application serves 12 states. Each state has 3-8 custom extensions (eligibility checks, claims validators, provider workflows). Extensions must load dynamically based on logged-in user's tenant. Static bundling would require all extensions loaded for all users regardless of tenant, resulting in a large combined bundle.

**Application**: Each state packages extensions as Module Federation remotes. Deploy to CDN at /extensions/{state}-{feature}/v{version}/. Extension Registry stores mappings: Texas tenant → 5 extension URLs, California tenant → 8 URLs, Florida tenant → 6 URLs. ClaimsPro queries registry with user's tenant ID at login. Dynamically imports tenant-specific extensions via import(url). User sees only their tenant's extensions. Bundle size: ClaimsPro host shared bundle + tenant-specific extensions only.

**Benefit**: Scalable multi-tenancy. Add new tenant without rebuilding host. Bundle size proportional to tenant's extensions (not all extensions). Independent versioning per tenant (Texas runs extension v2.1, California runs v2.4). Deployment isolation (Texas deployment doesn't trigger California regression testing).

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

**Monolithic Extension Bundling:**
- Extensions bundled into host application during webpack build
- Full product rebuild for any extension change (3-6 month release cycle)
- All extensions loaded for all users (bundle size grows with extension count)
- React (420KB), design system (320KB) duplicated in each extension bundle
- Version coupling: Extension v2.1 only works with host v6.3 (tight dependency)
- Rollback requires full application rollback (12-hour process, production risk)
- Many extensions break during host upgrades (version incompatibility)
- Texas sees California extensions in browser DevTools (IP exposure concern)

**Deployment Process:**
1. Developer commits extension code
2. Triggers full host application build (12 products × 3 environments = 36 builds)
3. Regression testing for all extensions (8 days)
4. Coordinated release window (quarterly, 3-month cycle)
5. Deploy host + all extensions together
6. Rollback requires reverting entire deployment

**Problems:**
✘ High customer escalation costs due to slow deployment
✘ Significant bundle duplication (shared dependencies duplicated per extension)
✘ Significant maintenance cost reworking extensions for host upgrades
✘ 12-hour rollback process; production outage risk
✘ IP exposure (all tenants download all extensions)

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

**Module Federation Extension Packaging:**
- Extensions packaged as independent Webpack remotes with versioned CDN URLs
- Extension deployment independent of host (2-day cycle)
- Tenant-specific dynamic loading (Texas loads Texas extensions only)
- React (420KB), design system (320KB) shared via singleton; loaded once
- Version flexibility: Extension v2.1 works with host v6.2-v6.4 (±1 minor version)
- Independent rollback: Change registry URL; 90-second rollback
- Compatible version ranges prevent breakage (<0.5% incompatibility rate)
- Tenant isolation: California cannot access Texas extension code (registry enforces)

**Deployment Process:**
1. Developer commits extension code
2. Extension-specific CI/CD pipeline builds only that extension (3-5 minutes)
3. Automated tests for extension only (20 minutes)
4. Deploy to CDN at versioned URL (1 minute)
5. Update Extension Registry API with new URL
6. Extension loads for configured tenants immediately
7. Rollback: Update registry to previous version URL (90 seconds)

**Outcomes:**
✓ Customer escalation costs reduced (2-day deployment cycle)
✓ 60% bundle size reduction (89% for California: 780KB → 87KB)
✓ 96% faster time-to-production (12 weeks → 3 days for California)
✓ 90-second rollback (vs. 12 hours); zero production outages
✓ Tenant IP isolation (registry enforces access control)

### Related Patterns

**[PTN-APP-EXT-014: UI Extension Point Registration](PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md)**
Defines registration mechanism for extensions to declare UI extension points. Federated modules register via Extension Registry API with metadata (name, version, exposed components, tenant, URL). Host queries registry; dynamically loads registered extensions.

**[PTN-APP-MTN-010: Tenant Extension Loading](../../multi-tenancy/PTN-APP-MTN-010-tenant-extension-loading-pattern.md)**
Defines backend service for managing tenant-to-extension mappings. Extension Registry (PostgreSQL database) stores tenant → extension URL mappings. REST API provides /extensions?tenantId={id} endpoint. PTN-APP-EXT-013 queries this API to fetch remote entry URLs for dynamic loading.

Defines tenant-specific micro-frontend loading at application shell level. Uses Extension Registry to determine which MFEs to load per tenant. PTN-APP-EXT-013 applies same pattern for extension-level components within MFEs. Both use Module Federation for runtime composition.

### Dependencies

**Build-Time Dependencies:**
- **Webpack 5.60+**: ModuleFederationPlugin for remote module configuration; container API for runtime loading
- **Node.js 18+ and npm 9+**: Build tooling; package management; script execution
- **TypeScript 4.5+**: Type safety for exported component interfaces; d.ts generation for consuming applications
- **React 18+ and React-DOM**: UI library for extension components; must match host version ±1 minor

**Runtime Dependencies:**
- **@gainwell/extensions-sdk-react v2.4+**: loadRemoteModule() helper function for dynamic import with error handling; ExtensionComponentProps interface
- **@gainwell/design-system-react v4.x**: Shared UI component library; marked as singleton in Module Federation config
- **Extension Registry API**: Backend service (REST API) mapping tenants to extension URLs; host queries at runtime

**Infrastructure Dependencies:**
- **Azure CDN**: Global content delivery network hosting remoteEntry.js + chunks; CORS headers configured
- **Azure DevOps**: CI/CD pipeline for automated build, test, deployment to CDN, registry API updates
- **Extension Registry Database**: PostgreSQL storing tenant-extension mappings; queried via API

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Customer extensions need to be packaged as independently deployable micro-frontend modules, but without standardized Module Federation configuration, dynamic loading and runtime composition is not possible.

**Solution:** Standardize packaging extensions as Webpack Module Federation remote modules with versioned entry points, shared dependencies, and dynamic loading capabilities.

**When to Use:** Packaging customer extensions as micro-frontends, dynamic tenant-specific UI loading, independent extension versioning, or multi-tenant SaaS with customer UI modules.

**Key Benefits:**
- Independent deployment cycles for extensions
- Runtime composition based on tenant context
- Efficient code sharing across modules

**Implementation Complexity:** High

**Prerequisites:** Webpack 5+ with Module Federation, Node.js 18+, CDN hosting, Module Federation understanding

**Related Patterns:** PTN-APP-EXT-003 (Package Management), PTN-APP-EXT-012 (React Components), PTN-APP-MTN-012 (Tenant MFE Loading)
